checks: Identify the caller identity for each entry and whether anonymous, low-privilege, tenant, and admin callers can reach the same operation.
Verify server-side authentication and default-deny behavior for every protected action; do not trust frontend checks or gateway-only checks.
Check object-level authorization for user-controlled IDs, parent IDs, tenant IDs, and owner fields, including read, update, delete, export, and batch variants.
Check horizontal and vertical authorization across sibling operations, internal endpoints, admin endpoints, bulk endpoints, and async workers.
Check authentication bypasses through alternate paths, case or encoding differences, duplicate parameters, trusted proxy headers, IP or Referer trust, and capture-replay.
Check session lifecycle: fixation, rotation, expiration, logout, remember-me, concurrent sessions, cookie scope, and SameSite behavior.
Check CSRF protection for state-changing requests, including JSON endpoints and requests that rely on ambient credentials.
Check JWT, OAuth, API-key, and signature validation: algorithm, key selection, signature, issuer, audience, expiry, state, redirect URI, and claim trust.
Check password recovery, MFA, invitation, registration, and account-linking flows for authentication bypass or account takeover.
Check default, shared, hard-coded, or example credentials and whether they are reachable in production.
Check whether the identity used by a security decision is the same identity used by the protected sink, including time-of-check/time-of-use changes.
Trace attacker-controlled values into SQL, HQL, JPQL, stored procedures, dynamic ORDER BY or LIMIT clauses, LIKE expressions, IN lists, and raw ORM fragments (CWE-89).
Check NoSQL and document-query operators, including MongoDB operators such as $ne, $gt, and $where, and GraphQL variables, directives, and resolver query construction (CWE-943).
Check ORM and query-builder misuse: raw fragments, dynamic table or column names, JSON paths, and query objects built from user-controlled maps.
Check OS command and shell injection through sh -c, pipes, redirection, command concatenation, environment variables, and user-controlled filenames or arguments (CWE-77/78).
Check argument injection even without a shell, including leading dashes, option order, URL schemes, and arguments that change a helper's behavior (CWE-88).
Check code and expression injection through eval, reflection, dynamic import, scripting engines, SpEL, OGNL, EL, and JNDI boundaries (CWE-94/917).
Check server-side template injection, user-controlled template names or fragments, expression evaluation in templates, and frontend/backend template boundary confusion (CWE-1336).
Check LDAP filter and DN construction, XPath and XQuery predicates, and XML construction or XSLT boundaries (CWE-90/643/652/91).
Check reflected, stored, and DOM cross-site scripting (XSS) across HTML, attribute, URL, JavaScript, CSS, and rich-text contexts, including cases where framework escaping is bypassed (CWE-79).
Check response header and CRLF injection through Location, Set-Cookie, and other headers, and log forging or structured-log field injection (CWE-113/93/117).
Check CSV and spreadsheet formula injection for exported values beginning with =, +, -, or @ (CWE-1236).
Check prototype pollution through object merges, __proto__, constructor.prototype, and deep-copy or deep-merge helpers (CWE-1321).
Check HTTP parameter pollution and parser differentials where duplicate parameters, arrays, or scalar conversions are interpreted differently by proxy, framework, and business code (CWE-235).
Check second-order injection after storage, normalization, decoding, or later re-parsing, and verify the effective grammar and escaping at the final sink.
Check path traversal and absolute path injection, including dot segments, encoded separators, null bytes, Windows separators, UNC paths, alternate data streams, and case differences (CWE-22/23/36).
Check canonicalization and path equivalence: whether the validated path is the same path used by the sink, including symlink, hardlink, and race behavior (CWE-41/59/61/62/64/65/66/67/69).
Check file inclusion and dynamic import through user-controlled paths, extensions, or protocols (CWE-98).
Check download, preview, static serving, and export paths for confinement to the intended root and for cross-tenant or cross-user access.
Check upload handling: extension, Content-Type, magic bytes, content parsing, dangerous file types, storage location, executability, and overwrite behavior (CWE-434).
Check archive extraction for zip slip, tar symlinks, path traversal, overwrite, destination escape, and decompression bombs (CWE-22/409).
Check temporary file creation, permissions, predictable names, atomic writes, cleanup, and umask (CWE-377/732).
Check file metadata and filename handling when values flow into logs, commands, SQL, templates, or response headers.
Check create, delete, rename, chmod, and directory creation operations for authorization and path confinement.
Check server-side request forgery through user-controlled URL, host, port, scheme, redirect, Unix socket, or DNS resolution, including IPv4, IPv6, decimal, octal, and IPv4-mapped forms (CWE-918).
Check that outbound allowlists are applied after DNS resolution and redirect handling, not only to the original string.
Check open redirects through return, next, callback, and protocol-relative URLs (CWE-601).
Check CSRF protection for state-changing cross-site requests, including cookie scope, SameSite, token validation, and Origin/Referer checks (CWE-352).
Check CORS policy for wildcard origins with credentials, reflected origins, and trusted subdomain assumptions (CWE-942).
Check HTTP request smuggling through Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding disagreement, plus frontend/backend parser differentials (CWE-444).
Check response splitting and header injection through CRLF in Location, Set-Cookie, and other headers (CWE-113/93).
Check Host header and forwarding-header trust, including X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded headers (CWE-644).
Check TLS certificate validation, protocol strength, and cleartext transmission (CWE-295/319/326/327).
Check WebSocket origin validation, callback and webhook trust, and internal-service reachability (CWE-1385).
Check unsafe deserialization across Java, PHP, Python, .NET, pickle, YAML tags, XML decoders, and custom serialization formats (CWE-502).
Check polymorphic type selection, reflection, object construction, and gadget-chain exposure after deserialization.
Check XML external entities, DTDs, XInclude, and schema validation boundaries (CWE-611).
Check JSON, YAML, protobuf, binary, and custom parsers for duplicate keys, type confusion, unknown fields, coercions, and unsafe defaults.
Check numeric conversions for overflow, truncation, signedness, length calculations, and index or size arithmetic (CWE-190/191/194/195/196/197/198/199).
Check encoding and Unicode normalization, including UTF-7, UTF-16, surrogates, case folding, and null bytes (CWE-20/116/170).
Check conversions between strings, paths, identifiers, and structured values that can change meaning before a security decision.
Check parser differentials where proxy, framework, validation layer, and business parser interpret the same input differently.
Check whether deserialized objects bypass validation or invoke constructors, magic methods, or callbacks with security impact.
Check source, configuration, tests, examples, scripts, CI, containers, and build artifacts for credentials, tokens, private keys, and connection strings (CWE-798/1392).
Check logs, error pages, stack traces, debug output, metrics, traces, source maps, exports, caches, and backups for sensitive values (CWE-200/201/203/209/215/532/538).
Check URL query strings, headers, cookies, local storage, and third-party callbacks for sensitive data exposure.
Check encryption at rest and in transit, password hashing, key derivation, random values, key rotation, and key scope (CWE-312/313/314/315/316/319/326/327/328/330/338).
Check tenant, user, and role isolation for sensitive records and whether responses apply least privilege and redaction.
Check data retention, deletion, backup, cache expiry, and CDN cache keys.
Check default or shared credentials and whether example credentials are reachable in production.
Do not contact external services or test real credentials; establish exposure from source and configuration only.
Check lifecycle transitions for create, submit, approve, cancel, complete, refund, and close; verify the order cannot be skipped, reversed, or replayed (CWE-840/841).
Check multi-step workflows for step skipping, replay, concurrent execution, duplicate callbacks, and out-of-order messages.
Check idempotency, retries, timeouts, rollback, and partial failure for inconsistent state.
Check business invariants for approval, quota, inventory, balance, coupons, and entitlements.
Check negative, zero, very large, fractional, and unit-conversion values that can bypass business limits.
Check ownership transfer, sharing, invitations, bulk operations, import, and export.
Check race conditions and time-of-check/time-of-use gaps; verify lock granularity and transaction boundaries (CWE-362/364/366/367).
Check mass assignment where user-controlled fields can change role, owner, status, price, or other protected attributes (CWE-915).
Check object-level authorization and tenant isolation in state-changing operations (CWE-639/862/863).
State the violated invariant and the capability obtained by the attacker, not just the workflow description.
Check limits on request bodies, files, fields, arrays, pagination, and nested objects (CWE-400/770).
Check decompression bombs, XML entity expansion, deeply nested structures, and recursive parsing (CWE-409/674/776).
Check regular-expression complexity and algorithmic complexity in sorting, deduplication, graph traversal, and query evaluation (CWE-407/1333).
Check unbounded fan-out, retry amplification, external-call amplification, and queue, thread, or connection-pool exhaustion (CWE-405/406/410).
Check memory, disk, CPU, file-descriptor, lock, and temporary-file consumption.
Check timeout, cancellation, backpressure, rate limiting, and quota coverage on slow paths.
Establish a bounded local effect; do not stress a live service.
Check configuration sources, defaults, environment overrides, precedence, and empty or invalid values (CWE-15/16/1188).
Check debug and admin features, example settings, default accounts, default keys, and default-disabled security controls (CWE-489/1188).
Check plugin, extension, dynamic import, classpath, and module-search behavior (CWE-829/830/912).
Check dependency versions, lock files, unmaintained or vulnerable dependencies, dependency confusion, and typosquatting (CWE-1104/1357/1395).
Check download, update, build, and release integrity verification (CWE-494/506/507).
Check CI/CD, container, startup scripts, permissions, and secret injection (CWE-250/732).
Check whether low-privilege users or external input can change security-relevant configuration.
Separate source-backed behavior from deployment facts; keep unconfirmed deployment conditions as gaps.
Check buffer copies, length calculations, and bounds checks for overflow and out-of-bounds access (CWE-119/120/121/122/125).
Check integer overflow, truncation, and signed/unsigned conversions that affect allocation or indexing (CWE-190/191/194/195/196/197/198/199).
Check array indexing, pointer arithmetic, off-by-one errors, and allocation-size multiplication.
Check null pointers, uninitialized memory, and error paths that leave objects partially initialized (CWE-476).
Check use-after-free, double free, lifetime, ownership, and error-path cleanup (CWE-415/416).
Check unsafe casts, FFI, JNI, native bindings, and serialization boundaries.
Establish a concrete integrity or isolation impact; do not report theoretical memory issues without evidence.
After the baseline categories, search for a security-relevant invariant, trust boundary, or business rule that the baseline does not cover.
Follow the strongest source-backed lead and record a new category or an explicit negative scope.
Do not treat open exploration as a replacement for required baseline category records.
Do not record an empty result as proof of security.
